body.x: NOEOTE Co., Ltd., led by CEO Youngseok Oh, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Gyeonggi Pavilion, to demonstrate CogniTrack, a digital cognitive healthcare solution that screens cognitive status in under 30 seconds using only smartphone touch patterns and PC mouse trajectories, with no expensive equipment.

The company will be at Venetian Eureka Park, Booth 63312-18. CogniTrack estimates where a user is looking from touch and mouse movement alone, without an expensive eye tracker. Beyond scoring answers as right or wrong, it classifies users into five psychological states: confidence, hesitation, illusion, indifference and confusion. Ontology and knowledge-graph structures combined with generative AI automatically generate questions tailored to each user's personal and work context. A test that conventionally takes 20 to 30 minutes now takes under 30 seconds, which makes large-scale screening possible in hospitals, homes and workplaces, and repeated measurements allow early screening of people at high risk of mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Because the system measures whether a user truly knows something rather than simply marking answers right or wrong, the company says it can pick up early signs of cognitive decline. At the booth, NOEOTE will show the five-state analysis, calculation of a Brain Health Index (BHI) and personalized memory training built on ontology and generative AI.

NOEOTE is a cognitive healthcare startup founded in 2026. It was spun off from NAITEDU Co., Ltd., which owns metacognitive measurement technology for education, as a joint venture between En4U Technology Holdings, backed by Ajou University, and Kaiser Group, a bio-specialized holding company. It is pursuing clinical validation with Ajou University's convalescent hospital, and its business model spans B2C subscriptions, B2B corporate licensing, and B2G and B2B2H partnerships with hospitals and local governments. The company has three patent filings for its lightweight eye-tracking and metacognition measurement technology and a clinical advisory network at Ajou University that includes Cheolho Kim, a center director at Ajou University Hospital.

NAITEDU generated KRW 400 million in revenue in 2025 from its educational metacognition platform and has 5,000 cumulative users in Korea. Building on that base, NOEOTE expanded into cognitive healthcare and is upgrading its minimum viable product (MVP). It is in talks with Ajou University's convalescent hospital on a proof-of-concept (PoC) project for early MCI detection and with Suwon and Gwangmyeong on dementia prevention programs.

NOEOTE has no overseas revenue or export record so far. Japan is its first target market. Its aging rate is among the world's highest, demand for dementia and MCI management is strong, and preventive care and long-term care facilities are looking to digitize, which suits a subscription and B2B licensing model. NOEOTE plans to enter through Japanese-language support and participation in CEATEC, and it is looking for long-term care and nursing facility operators, local government preventive care program agencies, dementia-related medical institutions and neurology clinics, and Japanese insurance and healthcare IT distributors. The United States is second: through CES, the company wants to find long-term care operators, insurers and digital healthcare distribution partners, and it plans to expand later into Southeast Asia, where aging is advancing quickly. Its goals are PoC projects and investment from global care, insurance and healthcare partners.

The company plans to upgrade its MVP and launch a B2C app in 2026, then build clinical evidence in 2027 through a PoC at Ajou University's convalescent hospital, expanding from 50 to 100 participants, and pilots with three B2B companies. In 2028, it plans to add multilingual support and an API platform, consider overseas expansion and a local subsidiary, widen B2G and B2B2H contracts and pursue a Series A investment round. Software as a medical device (SaMD) and digital therapeutics (DTx) certification and privacy compliance are its heaviest burdens abroad, and it needs country-specific regulatory consulting and support for local certification and clinical costs. NOEOTE also asks for support with trade show participation, buyer matching and local PoC programs to secure partners and early references, and for translation, localization and global marketing support to cover multilingual user interfaces.

AVING News, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING News has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING News will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING News will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING News will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.

After CES 2027 concludes, AVING News will co-host a post-show conference with participating companies to highlight their achievements, strengthen their domestic visibility and enhance their corporate reputation.
